title: Inheritance and Leadership
overview: Numbers 27 addresses two pivotal moments in Israel’s wilderness journey: the daughters of Zelophehad petitioning for their father’s inheritance and the appointment of Joshua as Moses’ successor. This chapter highlights God’s justice in inheritance laws, ensuring the daughters receive their rightful portion, and underscores the importance of divinely appointed leadership for the community’s future. It bridges the transition from Moses’ leadership to Joshua’s, emphasizing obedience, continuity, and God’s sovereign guidance. These events reflect God’s care for justice within the community and His provision for orderly leadership, foundational for Israel’s entrance into the Promised Land.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: The Petition of Zelophehad’s Daughters.** The chapter opens with the daughters of Zelophehad approaching Moses and the assembly to claim their deceased father’s inheritance, as he had no sons. Their respectful appeal highlights a gap in inheritance law and raises a question of justice.

**Verses 6-11: God’s Judgment on Inheritance Rights.** God affirms the daughters’ claim and establishes a legal precedent for inheritance passing to daughters if no sons exist, then to brothers, and further kin, ensuring family property remains within the tribe.

**Verses 12-14: God’s Revelation to Moses about His Death.** God commands Moses to view the Promised Land from Mount Abarim but informs him that he will not enter it due to his earlier disobedience at Meribah.

**Verses 15-23: Appointment of Joshua as Moses’ Successor.** Moses intercedes for leadership continuity, asking God to appoint a leader to guide Israel. God instructs Moses to commission Joshua publicly, transferring authority and ensuring the people have a shepherd.

keyVerses.text: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.
keyVerses.significance: This verse establishes a divine precedent for inheritance rights of daughters, affirming justice and equity within God’s law. It highlights God’s concern for family legacy and property rights, correcting societal norms that excluded women from inheritance.

keyVerses.text: And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.
keyVerses.significance: This verse codifies the inheritance law revealed by God, ensuring daughters receive inheritance in the absence of sons. It reflects God’s provision for family continuity and social stability within Israel.

keyVerses.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Get thee up into this mount Abarim, and see the land which I have given unto the children of Israel.
keyVerses.significance: God’s command to Moses signals the impending end of his leadership and life, emphasizing the transition of leadership and the fulfillment of God’s promises to Israel.

keyVerses.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him;
keyVerses.significance: This verse marks the divine appointment of Joshua as Moses’ successor, highlighting the importance of spiritual gifting and God’s sovereign choice in leadership succession.

keyVerses.text: And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation.
keyVerses.significance: This verse underscores the role of divine guidance in leadership decisions, showing that Joshua’s authority is confirmed by priestly consultation with God, ensuring obedience to God’s will.

characters.name: Daughters of Zelophehad
characters.description: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah are the five daughters who boldly petition Moses for their father’s inheritance. Their faith and courage lead to a significant legal reform, demonstrating God’s justice and care for marginalized voices.

characters.name: Moses
characters.description: The leader of Israel who listens to the daughters’ plea, brings their case before God, and intercedes for leadership succession. His obedience and humility are evident as he follows God’s commands and prepares for the transition of leadership.

characters.name: God
characters.description: The sovereign lawgiver who affirms the daughters’ claim, establishes inheritance laws, reveals Moses’ fate, and appoints Joshua as the new leader. God’s justice, holiness, and providence are central in this chapter.

characters.name: Joshua
characters.description: Son of Nun, chosen by God and commissioned by Moses to succeed him. Described as a man ‘in whom is the spirit,’ Joshua’s leadership is divinely empowered and publicly affirmed.

characters.name: Eleazar the Priest
characters.description: The high priest before whom Joshua is set and who will provide divine counsel through the Urim. He represents the priestly mediation between God and Israel’s leadership.

themes.description: God’s response to the daughters of Zelophehad illustrates His commitment to justice, especially for those marginalized by cultural norms. This theme reflects the biblical principle that God upholds fairness and righteousness within the community.
The chapter highlights the importance of orderly leadership succession under God’s direction, ensuring continuity and obedience in guiding His people toward the Promised Land.
Inheritance laws in this chapter emphasize the covenantal promise to Israel regarding land possession, family legacy, and tribal identity, reinforcing God’s faithfulness to His covenant.
Moses’ impending death due to disobedience at Meribah serves as a sobering reminder of the necessity of obedience to God’s commands and the consequences of failing to honor Him.

historicalContext: Numbers 27 is set during the Israelites’ wilderness wanderings, approximately in the late 15th or early 13th century BC, depending on dating of the Exodus. The people are encamped near the border of the Promised Land, preparing to enter Canaan. Inheritance of land was central to Israelite identity and tribal organization, with property passing through male heirs, reflecting patriarchal customs common in the ancient Near East. The daughters’ petition challenges these customs, leading to a divinely mandated legal reform. Politically, Moses’ leadership is nearing its end, and the appointment of Joshua ensures a smooth transition of authority, crucial for maintaining unity and obedience as Israel faces conquest and settlement.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theologians emphasize God’s sovereign justice in affirming the daughters’ claim and the importance of covenantal inheritance. They see Joshua’s appointment as a clear example of God’s providential governance and the necessity of godly leadership for the church and nation.

Dispensationalists highlight the legal specificity of inheritance laws as part of God’s covenant with Israel, distinct from the church age. Joshua’s commissioning is viewed as a foreshadowing of Christ’s leadership and the future millennial kingdom.

Early church interpreters often saw the daughters of Zelophehad as types of the Church, inheriting God’s promises despite initial exclusion. Joshua’s succession prefigures Christ’s role as the true leader and shepherd of God’s people.

crossReferences.connection: Provides additional laws regarding inheritance and the rights of the firstborn, complementing the inheritance statutes given in Numbers 27.
Describes Joshua’s commissioning as leader of Israel, fulfilling the transition initiated in Numbers 27.
Speaks of God choosing David as shepherd of His people, paralleling the theme of divinely appointed leadership seen in Joshua’s commissioning.
Contrasts Moses’ leadership with that of Jesus, the ultimate faithful Son and leader, echoing the theme of leadership succession.
Affirms that in Christ there is neither male nor female, connecting to the theme of inclusion and inheritance rights exemplified by the daughters of Zelophehad.

application: Trust God’s justice to uphold what is right, even when cultural norms seem unjust.
Recognize the importance of orderly leadership and pray for those God has placed in authority.
Value the legacy of faith and responsibility to pass on spiritual inheritance to future generations.
Obey God’s commands fully, understanding that disobedience has serious consequences.
Stand courageously to advocate for justice and righteousness in your community.
Seek God’s guidance in all decisions, relying on His Spirit and counsel.
conclusion: Numbers 27 powerfully demonstrates God’s justice in addressing the needs of the marginalized and His providence in leadership succession. The daughters of Zelophehad’s faithful petition results in a lasting legal precedent, while Moses’ commissioning of Joshua ensures God’s people remain under divine guidance. This chapter calls believers to trust God’s righteous governance, uphold justice, and honor the leaders He appoints, all while faithfully obeying His commands as they journey in faith.

outline.heading: The Daughters of Zelophehad’s Petition
outline.description: The five daughters of Zelophehad approach Moses and the assembly to claim their deceased father’s inheritance, raising a question of justice and inheritance law.

outline.heading: God’s Judgment on Inheritance Laws
outline.description: God affirms the daughters’ claim and establishes a legal framework for inheritance passing to daughters if no sons exist, then to brothers and other relatives.

outline.heading: God’s Revelation to Moses about His Death
outline.description: God commands Moses to view the Promised Land from Mount Abarim but informs him he will not enter it due to prior disobedience.

outline.heading: Moses’ Intercession for Leadership
outline.description: Moses requests God to appoint a leader to guide Israel, emphasizing the need for a shepherd to prevent the people from being like sheep without a leader.

outline.heading: Joshua’s Commissioning as Leader
outline.description: God instructs Moses to lay hands on Joshua and publicly commission him before the priest and the congregation, transferring leadership authority.
